paragraphs: R’ Yudan bar Palya or Pilah.

Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:5 preserves his precious saying: “When He gave, He gave mercifully; when He took, He took mercifully. Not only that: when He gave, He did not consult a creature, but when He took, He consulted the court.” At the beginning of Sheviit, chapter 5, R’ Yudan bar Pedaya objects before R’ Yonah; Hyman says it SHOULD READ bar Pela, as in Pnei Moshe.

Hyman cites Shemot Rabbah 42:9 [פ״מבט in the supplied Hebrew] for R’ Yehudah ben Piluyah reporting R’ Meir, and Vayikra Rabbah 24:2 for R’ Yudan bar Pilya. He finds the Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot saying at the beginning of Midrash Tehillim, chapter 101, under the name R’ Yudan ben Palyya. In Tanchuma, Vayera 45, R’ Yehudah bar Palma asks, “What is Moriah?” Hyman says it SHOULD READ bar Palyah, as in the Prague printing.

notes.text: The checked Sheviit reads bar Pelaya, while Hyman reports Pedaya and prefers Pela; the forms remain distinct. Shemot Rabbah 42:9 confirms Meir and a Polvayah form, but the supplied locator פ״מבט remains irregular.

No new primary scalar was returned. Earlier reported Shemot 42:9/Polvayah/Meir and SheviitPelaya matches remain inherited bounded consultations, not fresh whole text inspections or proof of punctuation displacement in supplied פ״מבט. All supplied Palya/Pilah/Pedaya/Pela/Piluyah/Pilya/Palyya/Palma/Palyah forms remain distinct. Hyman says SHOULD READ both Pela and Palyah; the Prague and PeneiMoshe reading claims are not freshly collated. היתיב means OBJECTED, not sat, and רפ״ה is BEGINNING 5; רפ״קא is BEGINNING 101, not end. He DIDNOT consult a creature when giving and DID consult the court when taking, with both mercy clauses and NOTONLYTHAT retained. All personal titles, including contextual Meir, remain R-prime. The word Yerushalmi occurs explicitly for the saying later; this supports contextual corpus reading, not edition verification.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:5 has Yudan ben Palya and the two mercy clauses. In Sheviit 5:1 the objector is Yudan bar Palya (פליא), while the consulted Pnei Moshe comment calls him Yudan bar Pedaya. Hyman’s print proposes בר פליא, where the supplied Hebrew has בר פלא. The print’s Shemot Rabbah locator פ״מב־ט corresponds to 42:9, where Yehudah ben Polvayah speaks in Rabbi Meir’s name. The consulted Vayikra Rabbah 24:2 has Yudan ben Rabbi Pilya. Midrash Tehillim 101 in the consulted digital text has Yehudah bar Shila. Yitzchok Lowy’s comparison reports Yehudah ben Palyya in the Buber printing. The consulted Tanchuma Buber, Vayera 45, has Yehudah ben Palma. The Prague reading is Hyman’s report.
